Preventive Maintenance Preventive maintenance is a sub-program under the Asset Preservation Program that aims to preserve and prolong the lifespan of national roads. This program is typically carried out on roads that are in fair to poor condition, with the primary objective of preventing and delaying further deterioration to a state where extensive rehabilitation is necessary. Preventive maintenance aims to prevent and delay the deterioration of national roads to a bad condition where ultimately rehabilitation is reguired, which typically involves Asphalt Overlay, Asphalt Overlay with Correction, and Concrete Reblocking. Asphalt Overlay is done on roads in fair condition. It involves the application of an additional layer of asphalt, that covers imperfections in existing asphalt or concrete. It is commonly applied to pavement that hasminor damage like light cracking, mild deterioration, or slightly sunken areas. The process of overlaying asphalt commonly includes a leveling out of the old asphalt pavement, ensuring a smooth, even surface on which to add additional layers. Asphalt Overlay with Correction is done on roads in poor condition. It involves the repair of short intermittent damaged sections before applying asphalt overlay. For concrete roads, the most common type of corrective maintenance is a combination of concrete pavement restoration (CPR) in terms of the replacement of intermittent shattered slabs and asphalt overlay. Concrete reblocking is done on national roads in poor condition which involves selective reblocking or replacement of intermittent shattered slabs in bad condition. process aims to improve the pavement ' s load-bearing capacity, reduce the risk of potholes, and enhance the pavement ' s durability and longevity.

Rehabilitation / Reconstruction / Upgrading of Damaged Paved Roads The Rehabilitation, Reconstruction, and Upgrading of Damaged Paved National Roads is the sub-program aimed at restoring the national roads to an optimal condition. This sub-program under Asset Preservation Program targets national roads that are in poor condition and are no longer cost-effective to maintain. Upgrading from asphalt to concrete is also a part of this sub-program. This involves replacing the asphalt surface with a concrete one, which provides enhanced durability, resistance to heavy loads, and reduced maintenance costs.

This sub-program is designed to enhance the engineering design of national roads to withstand the impact of severe storms and natural calamities in support of climate change adaptation.

Construction / Upgrading / Rehabilitation of Drainage along National Roads The Construction, Upgrading, and Rehabilitation of Drainage along National Roads is a Sub-program under Asset Preservation Program aims to construct, improve, and rehabilitate drainage structures such as box culverts, pipe culverts, side drains, and lined canals along national roads to prevent flooding and water run-off on the road surface.

Asset Preservation Program The program aims to improve the quality of national roads to international standards and ensure resiliency to natural disasters. This program encompasses the preservation of the existing paved national roads through the following sub- programs: Preventive Maintenance; Rehabilitation / Reconstruction / Upgrading of damaged paved national roads; Rehabilitation / Reconstruction of National Roads with slips, slope collapse, and landslide; construction, upgrading / rehabilitation of drainage along national roads.

Construction of By-Pass and Diversion Roads This involves constructing new roads to bypass congested areas, reduce travel time, and provide an alternate route for motorists, which may be eligible for later classification into national roads through a series of criteria set by DPWH.

Construction of Missing Links / New Roads This involves constructing new roads in areas where there is no existing road network and where the existing road network is inadeguate, which may also be evaluated for potential classification as national roads based on DPWH ' s feasibility study and classification criteria. These new roads help to expand the road network and provide better connectivity.

Construction of Flyovers / Interchanges / Underpasses / Long Span Bridges These structures are essential in managing traffic flow at intersections with a high volume of vehicles. Flyovers, interchanges, underpasses, and long-span bridges help reduce congestion and improve traffic flow, especially in urban areas.

Paving of Unpaved Roads This involves the construction of a new pavement surface on unpaved national roads to improve road quality, increase national road capacity, and enhance the safety and comfort of road users.

Network Development Program The Network Development Program focuses specifically on the expansion and improvement of the national road network. It aims to expand the capacity of the national road network by constructing new roads that meet the functional classification criteria and improving the quality of existing national roads through various activities. Eligibility for later classification as a national road is determined by a feasibility study and the functional classification criteria set by DPWH. This is also achieved through a range of activities such as road widening, the construction of bypasses and diversion roads, the construction of missing links / new roads, the construction of flyovers, interchanges, underpasses, long-span bridges, off-carriageway improvement, and the paving of unpaved roads. The program includes several sub-programs aimed at achieving its objectives. These sub-programs include: Road Widening; Construction of By-Passes and Diversion Roads; Construction of Missing Links / New Roads; Construction of Flyovers / Interchanges / Underpasses / Long Span Bridges; Off-Carriageway Improvement; Paving of Unpaved Roads
